body.statement: For fixed \(C\in\mathcal D_G\) and \(D\in\mathcal D_H\), every observable mixture law generated from \(C\) by arbitrary independent centered nonconstant non-Gaussian finite-variance sources is generated from \(D\) if and only if there exist a surjection \(f:U_C\twoheadrightarrow U_D\) and nonzero scalars \(a_i\) with \(C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\) for all \(i\in U_C\). The necessity direction must use diagnostic centered finite-support sources in their original jump lattice and unique Laurent factorization; the sufficiency direction must merge independent sources and preserve non-Gaussianity.
body.justification: This theorem eliminates the unrestricted source-law quantifier without assuming overcomplete ICA recovery for a single law.
body.gap: Dai et al. compare observational distribution sets through mixing representations, but do not give this exact visible-source surjection criterion with invisible columns and irreversible source merging.
body.consumer: The population compiler can compare graph law sets using finite partition types rather than an unbounded search over source distributions.
body.proof_tex:
Apply the finite-mixture containment lemma with \(A=C\) and the candidate matrix \(D\).  Its source class is exactly the class in the present statement: independence, centering, nonconstancy, non-Gaussianity, and finite second moments are each imposed coordinatewise, and zero mixing columns are handled by independent arbitrary legal sources.  The lemma gives
\[
\mathscr L(C)\subseteq\mathscr L(D)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists f:U_C\twoheadrightarrow U_D\ \exists(a_i)_{i\in U_C}\in(\mathbb R\setminus\{0\})^{U_C}
\ \forall i\in U_C:\ C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}.
\]
Its necessity proof is the required diagnostic centered finite-support construction in the original free jump lattice \(\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z(r_iC_{:,i})\), and its Laurent factorization partitions rather than fractionally splits those generators.  Its sufficiency proof uses the same grouped source for every occurrence of a target column and proves, by the cited L\'evy--Cram\'er theorem, that each nonempty merged source remains non-Gaussian.  This proves both directions exactly, with invisible columns and source symmetries included.
